title: Junior Dev Jobs Are Down 20%… So Why Are Companies Hiring?
summary: HTML All The Things podcast on the junior squeeze: Stanford AI Index data, AI as layoff excuse, companies raising entry-level hiring.

assertions.quote: Employment among software developers aged 22 to 25 have has plummeted nearly 20% since 2024

verdicts.note: Stanford 'Canaries' (2025) found ~13% relative employment decline for 22-25-year-olds in AI-exposed jobs, but rates, over-hiring correction and other macro factors also matter.

assertions.quote: even as their older colleagues head count grows

verdicts.note: Hiring data (e.g. Stanford 'canaries' 2025) shows junior roles hit harder than senior, but evidence that senior demand rose is weaker.

assertions.quote: You're just blatantly just blaming layoffs on AI to make it seem like you didn't make the mistake of over-hiring

verdicts.note: Analyses (e.g. Oxford Economics, Challenger data) find AI is a small share of cited layoff reasons and some 'AI' cuts track cost cutting; but some cuts do reflect real automation.

assertions.quote: IBM, Cognizant, Cloudflare, Dropbox ... AI fluency is one of them

verdicts.note: IBM, LinkedIn, Cloudflare and others publicly announced more junior hiring in 2026, citing pipeline and AI fluency; still a minority of employers.

assertions.quote: you're not going to get any more any more seniors if you don't hire and train juniors

verdicts.note: A straightforward pipeline argument made by IBM and others; the long-run effect is unmeasured yet but well reasoned.

assertions.quote: they're also building new products, gathering client feedback, and talking to marketing teams

verdicts.note: The trend toward 'product engineers' and DevOps ownership predates AI; AI plausibly speeds it, but evidence is anecdotal.

assertions.quote: the more we democratize the creation of software ... the more companies that will require more people

verdicts.note: Jevons effects are historically common and plausible for software, but whether demand growth outpaces productivity for developer headcount is unproven.

assertions.quote: it's either heavily subsidized by the companies or it's just not usable in a general setting

verdicts.note: Heavy users clearly consume more compute than flat fees cover, which is why vendors added weekly limits; whether plans are below cost on average is not public.
